properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 9 at 11:49PM MST until November 10 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast New Mexico, Permian Basin, Davis
Mountains, and Marfa Plateau.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM MST /10 AM CST/ Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.
Patchy fog will drop visibility quickly over short distances.
Visibility may become severely restricted near rivers, bridges, and
other low-lying areas.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 9 at 7:45PM CST until November 10 at 3:00PM CST by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Llano River Near Mason affecting Mason County.

For the Llano River...including Junction, Mason...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Llano River near Mason.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding will occur.
Secondary roads and low water crossings will become flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CST Monday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 18.3 feet just after
midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage late
tonight.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 18.4
feet on 07/12/1988.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 745 AM CST.

properties.description:

properties.areaDesc: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 11:57AM CST until November 10 at 3:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 AM CST Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 9 at 11:18AM CST until November 10 at 10:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Pafford Crossing nr Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Pafford Crossing nr Comstock.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, (1.5 meters), Minor lowland flooding one
quarter mile wide at Pafford Crossing covers most of the right
bank. Turbulent flow above Pafford Crossing to Amistad Reservoir
can wash campers, automobiles, and equipment downstream.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:15 AM CST Monday the stage was 4.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 5.2 feet late this afternoon. It will
then fall below flood stage late this evening.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.1
feet on 09/23/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight CST.
